title: edge-auth-window-race-causing-soft-failures-and-backoff-overflow
creator: Maya Patel
description: During a regional capacity wobble, a narrow race between auth token lease refresh and our rate-limiter windowing logic caused a class of "soft failures": intermittent 429s and degraded success rates for several downstream tenants for ~45 minutes. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, temporary mitigations applied, and the prioritized follow-ups to eliminate the race and prevent backoff queue amplification under bursty auth churn.
impact_summary: Span: ~45m (2026-03-09 02:13–02:58 UTC). Affected: ~6% of total API traffic in us-west-2; certain high-throughput tenants experienced up to 30% elevated 429s and increased tail latency. Customer-reported errors and automated alerts triggered support escalations. No data loss; some requests were retried by clients, increasing overall load.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:13 UTC - Alert: surge in per-token 429s from the gateway, automated SLO dashboard flagged service-level error spike.
2026-03-09 02:16 UTC - On-call initiated bridge; initial hypothesis: quota enforcement misconfiguration or a throttling policy regressions after last deploy.
2026-03-09 02:23 UTC - Mitigation A: temporarily widened rate-limiter grace window on the most impacted zone to reduce false-positive enforcement.

2026-03-09 02:30 UTC - Investigation: correlation observed between auth lease refresh churn (short-lived tokens) and sudden drops in token-score cache hits leading to enforcement logic treating tokens as new and cold.
2026-03-09 02:42 UTC - Mitigation B: rolled out a hotfix that added a short-lived lease-toleration flag to the quota enforcer to ignore token-state transitions under known churn patterns.
2026-03-09 02:58 UTC - Error rates returned to baseline; bridge stood down. Postmortem follow-up ticket opened.
2026-03-10 - Ticket created to track longer-term fixes and tests.
root_cause: A timing window between auth token lease expiry/refresh events and our quota-enforcer's token-state reconciliation caused tokens to appear 'new' to the rate limiter. New-token handling path applies stricter initial limits and a conservative backoff queue for retries. Under bursty token churn (caused by a misconfigured upstream certificate rotation job), the enforcer rapidly filled its backoff queue and amplified per-token enforcement decisions, producing a transient 429 storm.
immediate_mitigation: Widened the 'new-token' grace window in the quota enforcer config for the impacted region to prevent immediate false enforcement.
Enabled temporary token-state caching override to treat recently-seen tokens as warm for 60s.
Raised customer-facing rate limits for a small set of affected enterprise tenants after coordination with support to reduce user-visible errors.
Deployed a throttling-smoothing patch that caps the rate at which a single token can be moved into the backoff queue.
Added observability metrics to track token-state transitions and backoff-queue growth in real time.
follow_up_actions: (ENG) Implement a deterministic token-state reconciliation protocol: use monotonic lease counters persisted to the auth cache to avoid racey 'new vs expired' classification — owner: Diego Alvarez, ETA: 2 weeks.
(ENG) Add end-to-end load test that simulates large-scale token churn and verifies no backoff amplification — owner: Priya Rao, ETA: 3 sprints.
(ENG/Infra) Harden upstream cert rotation job to perform staggered refreshes and add health-check gating to prevent mass token invalidation — owner: Lukas Chen, ETA: 1 sprint.
(ENG) Introduce a token warmup heuristic in the quota enforcer that progressively ramps limits for tokens flagged as recently rotated, with telemetry gating — owner: Diego Alvarez, ETA: 3 weeks.
(PM/Support) Create runbook for customer mitigation steps and SLA communication template for repeated token-churn incidents — owner: Anika Suresh, ETA: 1 week.
(SRE) Add automated remediation playbook to detect backoff-queue growth and apply controlled grace-window widening automatically — owner: SRE team, ETA: 4 weeks.
(Security) Review to ensure deterministic reconciliation doesn't open token replay or lease-prolongation attacks — owner: Security, ETA: 2 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic token-state reconciliation implemented and code-reviewed.
Simulated token-churn load test shows <1% relative increase in 429s vs baseline under 2M token rotations/minute.
Backoff queue growth alerting added and an automated mitigation that reduces enforcement aggressiveness is operational in staging.
Runbook published and on-call trained; post-incident customer communication template approved by support and PM.
status_updates: 2026-03-10: Initial scoping completed; root cause hypothesis validated with replayed traffic.
2026-03-11: Design review held for deterministic reconciliation; security team flagged replay-window concerns.
2026-03-12: Temporary toleration config promoted to 2 regions while permanent fix is implemented.
2026-03-14: Begin implementation of reconciliation protocol; unit tests and integration test plan drafted.
notes: This incident surfaced a class of failures that are invisible in unit tests because they depend on co-occurring auth churn and rate-limiter state transitions. Consider adding chaos scenarios to the test matrix.
We should re-evaluate our client retry guidance: client-side indiscriminate retries during token churn can worsen amplification. PM to coordinate updated retry recommendations.
Keep an eye on related tickets that change token lifecycle semantics (eg. short-lived tokens A/B experiments).
